items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: the manager -- the production manager at that time was (unintelligible) Atkins. He came down and gave us support, you see. He helped the idea.

ctx.x: But he had like a shopping concession there where they could buy records, and you see the singing, see. So -- all right, so there we come in them. As I say, there, "Curley Colonel McDimple" has been down there about three years, into its third year. And at that time, the good father who is known as Boston Jimmy (unintelligible) his partner was alive, Ray Malone. He was very popular. He used to turn the -- he did the two life scientists. This Jeckle and Hyde dance. A story dancer he was.

So, we came in there, see. And as I say, it was 13 tap dancers. And we had like some wardrobe mistresses or something, you know. What do you call them. They did support performing. We had like a parade and so forth. And the manager -- the production manager at that time was (unintelligible) Atkins. He came down and gave us support, you see. He helped the idea. So, we told him what it was, but he already knew in other words, because we had -- he was returning the favor otherwise. By his being up there in the…

So, he came down. He gave us an idea on how to come into the processional through the audience, you know. And like it was Robert E. Lee. And when they got up there and went on stage, they went into something about Christopher Columbus. And it was a cast dance, you see. And the cast would dance and dance on, you know, and they'd then fade off and leave the Master of Ceremonies out there, which was me, myself, Chuck Green, you see.
